knowledge:
- key_parameters: <type=the format of taxonomic classification output ("extended" or "brief") ;; strand=the strand to search for taxonomic classification ("top" or "both") ;; threshold=the confidence threshold for taxonomic assignment ;; minCoverage=the minimum coverage of a tile/primer/probe within a target group ;; minGroupCoverage=the minimum coverage of a tile/primer/probe across all sequences in the group ;; maxPermutations=the maximum number of probe permutations allowed per target site>
- alternatives: <None mentioned in the documentation, though the package supports multiple sequence input types such as DNAStringSet, RNAStringSet, and AAStringSet depending on the biological molecule.>
- when_to_use: <Use when you need to train a custom taxonomic classifier on reference sequences, classify query marker gene sequences, design highly specific FISH probes or PCR primers for target taxonomic groups, or design and analyze oligonucleotide microarrays.>
- pitfalls: <Ensure all sequences are in the same orientation using OrientNucleotides before training a classifier. Gaps must be removed from sequences using RemoveGaps before classification. Problem sequences in the training set can degrade classifier performance and should be iteratively identified and removed using LearnTaxa's output.>

workflows.name: taxonomic_classification
workflows.intent: Train a taxonomic classifier on reference sequences and classify query sequences (DNA or Amino Acids).
input: rank_path (optional taxid text file containing taxonomic ranks)
fas (FASTA file of query sequences to classify)
workflows.stages: 1. Read training sequences and optional taxid file ;; 2. Remove gaps and orient nucleotides ;; 3. Extract taxonomic group labels ;; 4. Iteratively train the classifier using LearnTaxa and remove problem sequences ;; 5. Read and clean query sequences ;; 6. Classify query sequences using IdTaxa ;; 7. Plot and analyze taxonomic assignments
workflows.code:
seqs <- readDNAStringSet(seqs_path)
taxid <- read.table(rank_path,
	header=FALSE,
	col.names=c('Index', 'Name', 'Parent', 'Level', 'Rank'),
	sep="*", # asterisks delimited
	quote="", # preserve quotes
	stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
seqs <- RemoveGaps(seqs)
seqs <- OrientNucleotides(seqs)
trainingSet <- LearnTaxa(seqs[!remove],
	names(seqs)[!remove],
	taxid)
test <- readDNAStringSet(fas)
test <- RemoveGaps(test)
ids <- IdTaxa(test,
	trainingSet,
	type="extended",
	strand="top",
	threshold=60,
	processors=1)
plot(ids, trainingSet)

workflows.name: pcr_primer_design
workflows.intent: Design specific PCR primers targeting a specific group of sequences.
workflows.stages: 1. Import sequences into an SQLite database using Seqs2DB ;; 2. Add taxonomic identifiers using Add2DB ;; 3. Generate sequence tiles using TileSeqs ;; 4. Design primers using DesignPrimers ;; 5. Evaluate PCR efficiency using CalculateEfficiencyPCR
workflows.code:
Seqs2DB(fas, "FASTA", dbConn, "Streptomyces")
Add2DB(data.frame(identifier=desc, stringsAsFactors=FALSE), dbConn)
tiles <- TileSeqs(dbConn, add2tbl="Tiles", minCoverage=1)
primers <- DesignPrimers(tiles, identifier="avermitilis",

workflows.name: microarray_design_and_analysis
workflows.intent: Design microarray probes for OTUs and solve for OTU abundance using Non-Negative Least Squares (NNLS).
workflows.stages: 1. Read DNA sequences ;; 2. Calculate distance matrix using DistanceMatrix ;; 3. Cluster sequences using Treeline ;; 4. Generate consensus sequences for clusters using ConsensusSequence ;; 5. Design microarray probes using DesignArray ;; 6. Convert probes to a design matrix using Array2Matrix ;; 7. Solve for OTU abundance using NNLS
workflows.code:
dna <- readDNAStringSet(fas)
dMatrix <- DistanceMatrix(dna, verbose=FALSE)
clusters <- Treeline(myDistMatrix=dMatrix, type="clusters", cutoff=0.03, method="complete", verbose=FALSE)
conSeqs <- tapply(dna, clusters$cluster, ConsensusSequence)
conSeqs <- unlist(DNAStringSetList(conSeqs))
probes <- DesignArray(conSeqs, maxPermutations=2, numProbes=20,
	start=120, end=1450, verbose=FALSE)
A <- Array2Matrix(probes, verbose=FALSE)
x_out <- NNLS(A, b, verbose=FALSE)
